standard.title: Guided statistical investigations
standard.description: conduct guided statistical investigations involving the collection, representation and interpretation of data for categorical and discrete numerical variables with respect to questions of interest
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can collect data and create graphical representations (AC9M3ST01, AC9M3ST02). They have not yet completed a full investigation cycle end-to-end under teacher guidance.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students conduct guided statistical investigations: posing a question, collecting and representing data, and interpreting results for categorical and discrete numerical variables.

nodes.label: Posing investigable questions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a question of interest that can be investigated by collecting data, and state the variable(s) involved.
nodes.minimum_width: With teacher guidance, formulate one question of interest that can be investigated using data; identify the variable and its type.
nodes.typical_width: Formulate and refine questions of interest; identify relevant variables and their types; explain how data could be collected to answer the question.
wider: Compare several possible questions about the same context and evaluate which can be answered with available data
Explore questions of community or social relevance — e.g. questions about their school or local environment — connecting statistics to purposeful inquiry

response_modes.reason: Posing an investigable question requires understanding what makes a question answerable with data. The reasoning scaffold 'what would I need to collect to answer this?' needs to be made explicit.

nodes.hinge_reason: An investigable question with a clearly identified variable is the entry point for the investigation cycle in Node 2 — a question that cannot be answered by data collection, or where the variable is undefined, means the student cannot proceed to collection or interpretation meaningfully.
success_criteria: Students can state a question that can be answered by collecting data.
Students can identify the variable in their question and its type (categorical or discrete numerical).

nodes.label: Conducting the investigation cycle
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can complete a guided investigation cycle: collect data, represent it graphically, and make an interpretive statement about the results.
nodes.minimum_width: With teacher guidance, complete one investigation: collect data for a given question, create one graph, and write one sentence interpreting the result.
nodes.typical_width: Complete a guided investigation from question through data collection, representation and interpretation; compare results with classmates; discuss what the data shows.
wider: Conduct two investigations on similar questions with different groups/samples and compare findings — introducing the idea that data varies
Contribute findings to a class investigation combining data from multiple groups — experiencing aggregated data as more informative than individual samples

response_modes.reason: The investigation cycle integrates all prior statistics nodes. Students whose component skills are individually solid often still struggle with the cycle as a whole — the integration of posing, collecting, representing and interpreting requires coordination that needs guided practice.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Multi-group comparison and data aggregation are genuinely enriching — they introduce the concept of sampling variation and collective data, which are foundational statistical ideas that extend well beyond Y3.
success_criteria: Students can collect data, create a graph and make an interpretive statement as a connected investigation.
Students can explain how their interpretation relates back to the original question of interest.
